units.text: This manual shows how to find files that meet criteria you specify, and how to perform various actions on the files that you find. The principal programs that you use to perform these tasks are ⟦0⟧, ⟦1⟧, and ⟦2⟧. Some of the examples in this manual use capabilities specific to the GNU versions of those programs.
units.sourceHTML: This manual shows how to find files that meet criteria you specify, and how to perform various actions on the files that you find. The principal programs that you use to perform these tasks are find, locate, and xargs. Some of the examples in this manual use capabilities specific to the GNU versions of those programs.

units.text: See ⟦0⟧History⟦1⟧ for a history of ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧ and ⟦4⟧. The current maintainers of GNU findutils (and this manual) are Bernhard Voelker and James Youngman. Many other people have contributed bug fixes, small improvements, and helpful suggestions. Thanks!

units.text: To report a bug in GNU findutils, please use the form on the Savannah web site at ⟦0⟧. Reporting bugs this way means that you will then be able to track progress in fixing the problem.
units.sourceHTML: To report a bug in GNU findutils, please use the form on the Savannah web site at https://savannah.gnu.org/bugs/?group=findutils. Reporting bugs this way means that you will then be able to track progress in fixing the problem.

units.text: If you don’t have web access, you can also just send mail to the mailing list. The mailing list ⟦0⟧bug-findutils@gnu.org⟦1⟧ carries discussion of bugs in findutils, questions and answers about the software and discussion of the development of the programs. To join the list, send email to ⟦2⟧bug-findutils-request@gnu.org⟦3⟧.
